## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vijayātherīgāthā* (Thig 6.8) is a short canonical poem in the Therīgāthā collection of the Pali Canon, consisting of verses 169–174 attributed to the elder nun (therī) Vijayā [SuttaCentral; Bingenheimer]. In modern scholarship, English translations of the text have been produced by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Scholars have noted textual and transmission anomalies regarding the verses associated with Vijayā. While many poems in the Therīgāthā display close parallels to corresponding verses in the Bhikkhunī Saṁyutta of the Saṁyutta Nikāya (SN), Marcus Bingenheimer highlights that Vijayā's verse in the SN is completely different from her Therīgāthā verses (vv. 169–174), and the commentary on the SN provides no information about her [Bingenheimer].

SuttaCentral records no curated external parallels for the text [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus detects significant Pali-internal reuse between the *Vijayātherīgāthā* and its traditional commentary, the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §1.1–7.1 with §2602–2618) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies formulaic text reuse with the immediately following poem of the elder nun Uttarā (*Uttarātherīgāthā*, Thig 7.1, segments §3.4–5.4 aligning with §3.4–6.2) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus registers no cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan literature meeting the reporting threshold [DharmaNexus].
